records.behaviour: Backend set present in the exact deployed ReXGlue GPU artifact versus pinned Canary source

rexglue.summary: The pinned source contains D3D12 and Vulkan, but the verified rexgpu-xenos.dll was built with D3D12 enabled and Vulkan disabled.

canary.summary: Pinned Canary source exposes D3D12, Vulkan and null factories, with platform and configuration selection.

material_divergences: The exact Fable deployment can execute only the ReXGlue D3D12 backend; Canary source comparison spans additional backends that are not in that artifact.

historical_provenance.summary: The plugin extraction explains deployment form; exact backend inclusion is confirmed by G1.5A CMake-cache and binary evidence rather than commit intent.

evidence: The staged, package and SDK-build DLL hashes match, and accepted logs identify D3D12 initialization.
evidence_required: No evidence is needed for active backend identity; behavior-level relevance belongs to individual rows.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Active-artifact claims must be restricted to D3D12; Vulkan differences are design reference only in this phase.

records.behaviour: Shared GPU architecture and D3D12/Vulkan/null capability boundaries

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue shares GPU modeling above D3D12/Vulkan backends and contains MoltenVK adaptations; it has no Canary null backend and current Fable packaging excludes Vulkan.

canary.summary: Canary retains shared GPU behavior above D3D12/Vulkan and a null backend, with provider capability branches and current per-backend implementations.

material_divergences: Backend inventory, host capability surfaces and MoltenVK-specific adaptation differ; these are not a ranking of implementation correctness.

historical_provenance.summary: ReXGlue's direct commit records its MoltenVK adaptations and runtime-discovery packaging.

evidence: Vulkan and null are excluded from the exact active GPU artifact.
evidence_required: None for the current artifact; future backend work would require a new scope and pin.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Backend-neutral guest behavior should be isolated from host API and capability choices; no backend expansion is authorized here.

records.behaviour: GPU construction, runtime ABI, ownership and dispatch

rexglue.summary: ReXApp loads rexgpu-xenos at runtime, creates an IGraphicsSystem through the plugin ABI, and retains runtime-side ownership and shutdown control.

canary.summary: Canary selects and owns an in-process D3D12, Vulkan or null GraphicsSystem factory as part of Emulator setup; it has no ReXGlue plugin ABI.

material_divergences: ReXGlue introduces a runtime-loaded GPU plugin ABI and IGraphicsSystem integration boundary absent from Canary.

historical_provenance.summary: Direct ReXGlue commits route GPU access through IGraphicsSystem and extract the Xenos implementation into a runtime-loaded plugin.

evidence: Accepted G1.5A runtime evidence identifies the loaded rexgpu-xenos.dll and D3D12 initialization path.
evidence_required: No additional evidence is needed to establish boundary use; defect relevance remains a separate G1.5D question.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Any renderer must implement the ReXGlue ABI and lifecycle contract even if guest-GPU semantics are derived elsewhere.
open_questions: Which ABI surface is the minimum stable native-renderer contract?

records.behaviour: Presentation and guest-GPU initialization, memory callbacks, interrupts, register ownership and shutdown

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue splits presentation from guest-GPU setup, embeds the register file, connects runtime memory and interrupt callbacks through IGraphicsSystem, and shuts down through the plugin owner.

canary.summary: Canary performs one GraphicsSystem setup sequence and allocates the register file in guest-addressable fixed memory while using Emulator-owned memory and interrupt facilities.

material_divergences: Initialization phases and register-file storage ownership differ; the callback and interrupt plumbing terminate in different host integration layers.

historical_provenance.summary: ReXGlue history directly records the setup split and IGraphicsSystem routing, but does not claim a guest-visible correction.

evidence: The accepted run reaches plugin setup, interrupt registration and frame presentation.
evidence_required: G1.5D must determine whether any lifecycle detail affects Fable rather than merely hosting it.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Preserve ReXGlue ownership and callback boundaries; Canary's allocation and setup shape is not directly portable.

records.behaviour: Accuracy, performance, cache and host-capability defaults

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue defaults anisotropic_override to 3 and clear_memory_page_state to true, exposes ReX-specific hot-reload and diagnostic controls, and gates selected compatibility/performance paths.

canary.summary: Canary defaults anisotropic_override to -1 and clear_memory_page_state to false and has a different current set of accuracy/performance and capability switches.

material_divergences: Default filtering, memory-validity refresh and several optional execution paths differ even when source algorithms are otherwise shared.

historical_provenance.summary: ReXGlue history explains its current single-validity state and a gated resolve pre-mask, but not every default-policy divergence.

evidence: The active ReXGlue DLL necessarily consumes its defaults unless overridden; the exact run-047 effective values were not recorded for every setting.
evidence_required: Effective CVar snapshot for the accepted Fable run and affected-path reachability.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Comparisons and future designs must pin effective settings as well as source revisions; defaults are not neutral.
open_questions: Which non-default GPU settings, if any, were active in Run 047?

records.behaviour: Ring reads, type-0/type-1/type-2/type-3 PM4 decoding, indirect buffers and XE_SWAP dispatch

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue keeps ring execution and PM4 handlers largely in one CommandProcessor translation unit.

canary.summary: Canary splits the same ring worker and templated PM4 handlers between CommandProcessor and pm4_command_processor_implement.h.

historical_provenance.summary: Current call-chain comparison found the same meaningful PM4 opcode coverage; file movement alone is not a material divergence.

evidence: sub_82BA34D8 calls VdGetSystemCommandBuffer and VdSwap; VdSwap emits PM4_XE_SWAP.
evidence_required: Per-opcode title use beyond XE_SWAP remains for G1.5D.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: A native renderer needs equivalent packet semantics, not Canary's current file split.

records.behaviour: Waits, events, interrupts, coherency requests and operation triggers

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue evaluates waits, writes events, invokes interrupts and accepts invalidate/coherency operations, with explicit incomplete coherency work.

canary.summary: Canary retains equivalent wait, event, interrupt and coherency dispatch behavior, including the same incomplete useful cache invalidation work.

historical_provenance.summary: No material current divergence was established; shared TODOs are retained as limitations.

evidence: No accepted title-specific packet stream identifies these affected operations.
evidence_required: A later read-only packet/capture observation or guest-code proof of the relevant opcodes.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Shared incompleteness should remain explicit rather than being mistaken for a Canary/ReXGlue divergence.
open_questions: Which coherency operations does Fable II emit?

evidence: This is host diagnostic capability, not guest execution behavior; this audit added no capture or instrumentation.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Canary trace tools may remain external references; their absence does not authorize porting or runtime instrumentation.

records.behaviour: Assertions, unsupported guest behavior, fallbacks, device loss and TODO policy

canary.summary: Canary has broadly equivalent error/device-loss and unsupported-operation handling, plus newer per-feature diagnostics; exhaustive semantic equivalence was not proven for every assertion and TODO.

historical_provenance.summary: A ReXGlue commit confirms one device-removal fix in its query path; broad diagnostic ancestry is not established.

evidence: No current first blocking failure is a GPU device-loss or unsupported-operation diagnostic.
evidence_required: A specific Fable failure and exact source path before narrowing this broad row.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Unsupported behavior must fail visibly and specifically; broad fallback transplantation is not justified.

records.behaviour: Draw initiation, primitive and index handling, extents and predication

canary.summary: Canary retains the same general draw-normalization chain with later special cases recorded separately.

evidence_required: Specific topology, predication and query use still requires G1.5D evidence.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: The common normalized draw contract is a useful behavioral decomposition, without selecting an implementation architecture.

records.behaviour: EVENT_WRITE_ZPD occlusion-query lifecycle and result retirement

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue's active D3D12 path holds one host query, ends/resolves/waits synchronously, and can fall back to a fixed fake sample count.

canary.summary: Canary owns a shared logical report lifecycle spanning submissions and passes, segmenting and asynchronously retiring D3D12/Vulkan host-query or counter-buffer results with fast, strict and fake modes.

material_divergences: Canary supports multi-segment, same-slot-reuse and asynchronous report lifetimes; ReXGlue's active path is a single synchronous D3D12 query lifecycle.

historical_provenance.summary: Canary documents the new logical report design; ReXGlue history documents its backend port and two local D3D12/sentinel corrections.

evidence: No accepted evidence identifies Fable ZPD packets or query-slot reuse.
evidence_required: Fable packet evidence for EVENT_WRITE_ZPD and the report lifecycle it exercises.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Query state should be specified as guest-visible report lifetimes before choosing host query mechanisms.
open_questions: Does Fable use ZPD, and if so does it span submissions or reuse report slots?

records.behaviour: Shared-memory watches, validity, upload/download, barriers, queues, fences and resource lifetime

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue maintains physical-page validity and watches, upload/download ownership, D3D12 transitions, submissions, fences and deferred resource release.

canary.summary: Canary retains the same broad watch/validity/upload/download and D3D12 submission/fence model, with invalidation lifecycle differences recorded separately.

historical_provenance.summary: ReXGlue removed its own double-buffered validity experiment; current broad validity ownership is equivalent, while unwatched invalidation remains separate.

evidence: Rendered output necessarily consumes uploaded guest resources and synchronized submissions.
evidence_required: Specific resource and transition evidence is still needed for any defect claim.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Coherency ownership and lifetime boundaries must be explicit across the runtime/plugin interface.

records.behaviour: Invalidation callbacks for unwatched decommit, release and protect-to-writable ranges

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue's callback path returns without firing when no watched bits are armed, including lifecycle changes on otherwise unwatched ranges.

canary.summary: Canary raises invalidation callbacks for decommit, release and protect-to-writable even if no watch is armed; it also resolves access at system-page granularity and validates unwatched write faults.

material_divergences: Canary invalidates GPU-side consumers on unwatched mapping lifecycle changes that ReXGlue's callback gate can omit.

historical_provenance.summary: The Canary commit explicitly combines system-page access, write-fault validation and unwatched lifecycle invalidation; only the last remains materially divergent from current ReXGlue in this row.

evidence: No affected Fable resource has been tied to an unwatched decommit/release/protect transition.
evidence_required: Guest allocation lifecycle and GPU cache state for an affected address range.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Mapping lifecycle invalidation must not depend solely on currently armed write watches.

records.behaviour: Pipeline descriptions, descriptor/binding layouts, specialization, keys and invalidation

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue derives pipeline descriptions and hashes from translated shaders, render-target and fixed-function state and manages descriptor/root binding invalidation.

canary.summary: Canary retains the same broad state-description, hashing, root-signature and binding pipeline with later state fields and capability paths separated below.

historical_provenance.summary: Equivalent current state assembly was established at the behavior level.

evidence: Rendered frames prove pipeline and binding assembly runs.
evidence_required: Affected pipeline keys and bindings remain unidentified.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Cache keys must encode every guest-semantic and host-capability input that changes generated behavior.

records.behaviour: Asynchronous D3D12 shader and pipeline creation

symbols: Await creation of all queued pipelines

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue may skip the initiating draw while a pipeline is unavailable, then drains queued work and waits for busy creation threads at submission end.

symbols: Draws will be skipped until pipelines are ready

canary.summary: Canary leaves creation running across submissions and skips every draw whose pipeline remains unavailable, re-fetching the root signature when ready.

material_divergences: ReXGlue bounds missing draws to the current submission by waiting at its end; Canary prioritizes lower frame-time stalls and may skip across submissions.

historical_provenance.summary: Pinned Canary source explicitly states the no-wait/skipped-draw performance rationale; the exact origin commit is unavailable within the shallow history.

evidence: No accepted evidence ties the black character surfaces to skipped pipeline creation, and the active CVar value for the affected frame is not established here.
evidence_required: Active async setting plus pipeline hashes/readiness for affected draws.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Async policy is guest-visible when draws are skipped; correctness and warm-up behavior must be specified before performance tuning.
open_questions: Were affected Fable draws skipped due to a pending pipeline?

records.behaviour: D3D12 constant-alpha blend factors on hosts without alpha-factor support

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue maps guest constant-alpha through the common blend factor and sends the four independent RB_BLEND values without a provider capability branch.

canary.summary: Canary uses D3D12 alpha-factor enums when supported and emulates alpha-only constant factors through the common factor on older hosts.

material_divergences: On hosts lacking D3D12 alpha-factor support, an alpha-only constant can use a different factor component in ReXGlue.

historical_provenance.summary: The direct Canary commit identifies the RTV constant-alpha correction; its one-line message does not provide broader title rationale.

evidence: No affected Fable blend state or host alpha-factor capability result has been recorded.
evidence_required: Host capability plus RB_BLENDCONTROL and RB_BLEND_ALPHA/color values for an affected draw.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Host blend capabilities must be represented in pipeline behavior and cache keys where they change factor semantics.

records.behaviour: XE_SWAP request, mailbox publication, guest-output refresh, present, resize and shutdown

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue routes XE_SWAP through backend IssueSwap and TextureCache into a mailbox-style Presenter, then composes runtime UI and presents through D3D12.

canary.summary: Canary uses the same guest swap-to-mailbox-to-provider-present chain within its monolithic UI ownership.

historical_provenance.summary: The guest-visible swap chain is equivalent; surrounding UI ownership differs but does not change the compared swap behavior.

evidence: sub_82BA34D8 [0x82BA34D8,0x82BA3BFC) calls VdSwap; Run 047 proves presented frames.
evidence_required: No additional evidence for swap reachability; presentation is not implicated in the black surfaces.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: The ReXGlue presenter/UI boundary must remain compatible, but swap equivalence supplies no implementation choice by itself.

records.behaviour: Guest vblank generation, counters and host frame limiting

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue creates a guest VSync thread from the configured video mode and catches up missed intervals in a while loop independently of presentation.

canary.summary: Canary runs a title-aware host frame limiter controlled by framerate_limit/vsync, increments D1MODE_V_COUNTER, and uses host sleep/spin pacing.

material_divergences: Timing source, configuration, counter handling, title-open gating and catch-up behavior differ.

historical_provenance.summary: ReXGlue directly records its catch-up pacing correction; the full divergence's earlier ancestry is not established in the available Canary shallow history.

evidence: Successful initialized rendering necessarily runs the ReXGlue guest-vblank thread; no symptom is attributed to its pacing.
evidence_required: Only needed if G1.5D investigates timing-sensitive behavior rather than the current visual defect.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Guest vblank semantics and optional host pacing should be separate policies.
open_questions: Which vblank counter behavior does Fable observe?

records.behaviour: Register-file reset values

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue zeroes the register file at construction and does not seed nonzero Xenos reset defaults.

canary.summary: Canary zeroes the file and then seeds confirmed nonzero retail-hardware context-register defaults, intentionally excluding tessellation levels.

material_divergences: Reads before a guest write return zero in ReXGlue but a nonzero hardware reset value for the registers initialized by Canary.

historical_provenance.summary: The Canary commit records retail-console reads corroborated by AMD and Mesa defaults and explains the deliberate tessellation omission.

evidence: Fable initializes the GPU, but no evidence shows it reads an affected register before writing it.
evidence_required: TU1 command/register-write ordering for every affected default read.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Hardware reset state is an explicit guest contract candidate, but the exact table and title reachability need independent validation.
open_questions: Does Fable depend on any seeded reset value?

records.behaviour: Register writes, fetch-constant dirty ranges and operation-triggered state invalidation

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue writes the register file and propagates dirty state to shaders, texture fetches, samplers and fixed-function state.

canary.summary: Canary propagates the same categories of register and fetch-constant invalidation through reorganized current code.

historical_provenance.summary: The pinned implementations have equivalent current bulk-fetch invalidation boundaries; older fixed history is not a current divergence.

evidence: Rendered frames require register writes and dirty-state consumption, though no specific defect is attributed here.
evidence_required: No additional evidence for broad use; per-register relevance remains unknown.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Preserve dependency-level invalidation rather than copying either implementation's container layout.

records.behaviour: Host-RT and interlock ownership, MSAA surfaces, copies, clears, resolves and EDRAM alias tracking

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue implements host-render-target and ROV paths, tile ownership and overlap transfer, depth/color clears, resolves and cache invalidation.

canary.summary: Canary retains the same broad host-RT/interlock, ownership, transfer, clear and resolve model, with layout and conversion corrections recorded separately.

historical_provenance.summary: The common architecture is semantically equivalent at this comparison granularity.

evidence: Run 047 proves rendered and presented color/depth content, but not which EDRAM subpaths produce the black character surfaces.
evidence_required: Per-pass render-target formats, sample counts and resolves for affected draws.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: EDRAM ownership and alias handling remain mandatory behavioral areas even where structure differs.

records.behaviour: Canonical 1x, 2x and 4x EDRAM sample addressing

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue uses the older sample layout and pair-specific transfer assumptions.

canary.summary: Canary canonicalizes guest sample coordinates in 4x4 blocks for 1x, 2x and 4x and applies that scheme across resolves, clears, transfers, dumps and interlock paths.

material_divergences: Aliased views, MSAA sample positions and transfers address different EDRAM locations for affected patterns.

historical_provenance.summary: The commit provides the new address equations and explains why the old 2x2 subdivision shuffled aliased views.

evidence: No affected Fable pass has been shown to reinterpret or resolve an MSAA layout in the divergent pattern.
evidence_required: Affected pass sample count, EDRAM bases/pitches, aliasing and resolve coordinates.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: A renderer needs a single validated Xenos EDRAM address model shared by all operations.
open_questions: Do the black surfaces originate in an aliased or multisampled pass?

records.behaviour: Readback of resolution-scaled resolves

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue's D3D12 readback rereads destination state and copies using the older scaled range and written-length handling.

canary.summary: Canary uses ResolveInfo-derived format/size, binds the written extent, validates group alignment and committed writable destination, rejects unsupported ranges, and truncates non-whole-tile tails.

material_divergences: Source window, destination interpretation, validity guards and tail handling differ for scaled resolve readback.

historical_provenance.summary: Canary's commit explicitly documents the downscale-CS contract; ReXGlue later gated an independent pre-mask behavior for a non-Fable title issue.

evidence: No accepted Fable evidence identifies resolution-scaled resolve readback for an affected resource.
evidence_required: ResolveInfo, scale, written extent and subsequent shared-memory consumer for the affected pass.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Scaled resolve storage and readback need an explicit layout/validity contract; ReXGlue's configurable pre-mask is not a general correctness conclusion.

records.behaviour: 8_8_8_8_GAMMA and fixed-number resolve conversion

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue lacks Canary's PWL gamma decode during resolve and its copy_dest_number-dependent fixed destination packing.

canary.summary: Canary unconditionally enables 8_8_8_8_GAMMA EDRAM piecewise-linear decode before resolve/conversion and packs fixed destinations according to copy_dest_number.

material_divergences: Gamma-space values and fixed destination component packing differ for the affected resolve formats.

historical_provenance.summary: The introducing commit records both resolve changes and initially default-enables PWL decoding; a later direct commit removes the decode/num_format CVars, leaving the pinned behavior unconditional.

evidence: No affected Fable resolve format or copy_dest_number is known.
evidence_required: Fable resolve source/destination formats, copy_dest_number and consumer.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Resolve conversion should be format-exact and separate from host sRGB assumptions.

records.behaviour: Extended-range Xenos float16 render-target and memexport packing

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue retains a TODO for universal extended-range encoding and uses host float16 behavior in affected pack/unpack paths.

canary.summary: Canary treats exponent 31 as finite up to 131008 in render-target and memexport pack/unpack rather than host Inf/NaN semantics.

material_divergences: Values above 65504 and exponent-31 encodings differ in clamp, pack and unpack behavior.

historical_provenance.summary: The commit explicitly identifies the guest exponent-31 finite range and the old clamp/Inf behavior.

evidence: No affected Fable render target, memexport format or value range is identified.
evidence_required: Fable formats and value evidence reaching extended float16 encodings.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Guest float formats require explicit bit-level semantics independent of host IEEE shortcuts.

records.behaviour: Shader loading, microcode parsing, control flow, constants, fetches, exports, host generation, hashes and caches

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue hashes and analyzes Xenos microcode, translates control flow, constants, fetches and exports, compiles host shaders, and persists shader/pipeline descriptions.

canary.summary: Canary retains the same broad analysis, translation, hashing and cache chain, with material instruction changes recorded separately.

historical_provenance.summary: High source ancestry and direct call-chain tracing support equivalence at this granularity; no source-body copy is included.

evidence: Run 047's rendered output requires working guest shader analysis and host shader execution.
evidence_required: Affected character shader identities remain required for defect mapping.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Instruction and export semantics, hashes and cache invalidation are separate renderer contracts even if implementation structure changes.

records.behaviour: Scalar approximation precision versus a title-specific tessellation workaround

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue retains a legacy title-ID-specific quad-domain index/coordinate workaround and lacks Canary's generalized scalar-result precision reduction.

canary.summary: Canary removes that AC6-specific workaround and rounds EXP/LOG/RCP/RSQ/SQRT-family scalar results to 21 mantissa bits in translators and interpreter.

material_divergences: The implementations modify different operations: ReXGlue changes a title-specific tessellation input while Canary changes a family of scalar ALU results globally.

evidence: The referenced 4D5307F2 and 4E4D07D1 title cases are not Fable II; no Fable scalar-sensitive shader is identified.
evidence_required: Affected Fable shader microcode and value comparison showing sensitivity to these operations.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Neither title-specific workarounds nor unconfirmed generalized precision should be adopted as Fable policy without independent evidence.
open_questions: What are the exact Xenos scalar approximation precision and halfway rules?

records.behaviour: Texture keys, layout, tiling, endian conversion, caching, residency, aliases, watches and sampler binding

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue derives guest texture layout and keys, tracks base/mip residency and memory watches, uploads endian/tiling-converted data, and binds cached textures and samplers.

canary.summary: Canary retains the same broad cache, watch, layout, upload and binding architecture, with material format and invalidation changes recorded separately.

historical_provenance.summary: Equivalent behavior was traced through shared and D3D12 call chains; later special cases are separate records.

evidence: Run 047 contains correctly textured environment, UI and some clothing.

records.behaviour: Shared-memory validity check before declaring a texture current

records.behaviour: Dummy texture headers containing only literal swizzles

evidence: No Fable dummy texture header with only literal swizzles is identified.
evidence_required: Affected Fable fetch constants and binding-layout use.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Literal-only bindings may still carry dimension and binding-layout semantics.

records.behaviour: Tessellated triangle-strip and triangle-fan conversion

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue rejects tessellated triangle strips and fans; its tessellation path accepts triangle lists and supported patch forms.

canary.summary: Canary normalizes tessellated strips and fans to triangle-list host draws, constructing a conversion buffer at runtime when needed.

material_divergences: Canary executes two tessellated topologies that ReXGlue rejects.

historical_provenance.summary: The Canary commit explicitly describes topology normalization and runtime conversion-buffer construction.

evidence: Both trees contain a Fable title-ID comment for a quad-patch ground case, which is outside this strip/fan divergence.
evidence_required: TU1 draw topology evidence showing whether Fable emits tessellated strips or fans.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: Topology conversion requirements should be driven by observed guest draws; the known Fable quad-patch note does not prove this path matters.

records.behaviour: Vertex-fetch bounds and out-of-range lane values

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue's translators may load complete words beyond the fetch-constant size from shared memory.

symbols: Words at or past the end of the fetch buffer
Words at or past the end of the fetch buffer

canary.summary: Canary clamps words at or beyond the fetch-constant size to zero in both translators.

material_divergences: Out-of-range lanes can expose adjacent shared-memory contents in ReXGlue but are zero in Canary.

historical_provenance.summary: The commit states that zero is the real-hardware result.

evidence: No accepted shader/fetch evidence identifies an out-of-range Fable access.
evidence_required: Affected Fable vertex fetch instructions, fetch constants and indices.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: A renderer contract should define fetch bounds independently of host memory safety behavior.

records.behaviour: XPS physical heap and GPU L2 address wrapping

rexglue.summary: ReXGlue labels the 0x7F region as possible XPS but does not back it as a physical heap and does not wrap L2 fetch/index addresses to backing storage.

canary.summary: Canary maps 0x7F000000 through 0x7FC7FFFF as a physical heap and masks L2 addresses in vertex fetch, index and translator paths.

material_divergences: Canary provides real backing and address wrapping for XPS; ReXGlue does not.

historical_provenance.summary: The direct parent of the pinned Canary revision introduces the heap and the fetch/index/translator wraps.

evidence: No accepted Fable allocation or GPU address lies in the XPS range.
evidence_required: TU1 allocations or fetch/index addresses in 0x7F000000..0x7FC7FFFF.

records.preliminary_renderer_implication: XPS is partly a runtime memory-map obligation, so renderer responsibility must be separated from ReXGlue memory ownership.
open_questions: Is XPS reachable in Fable II TU1?
